answer: A quartz-hard stake bond secures every agent identity. Registering locks capital that cannot be lent or shifted to another identity; each vouching peer locks less behind the claim. If a cluster is later proven to share one controller, the protocol slashes every bond in it and pays honest attestors. A sybil attacker cannot mint free identities: each carries real, slashable cost and ties up capital rather than recycling it. Honest agents recover bonds after cooling, so entry stays open while multiplying identities meets a canyon of rising marginal expense; to forge trust burns capital.
